description: GTA 6 launches November 19, 2026. GTA V made $815.7 million in 24 hours. How much could GTA 6 make, is the $1 billion sick-day claim real, does Take-Two stock pop on launches, and what did $10 a day in Take-Two since GTA V turn into?

segments.vo: Eight hundred fifteen million dollars. In twenty-four hours. And that was the last one.

When Grand Theft Auto Five came out in September 2013, it made eight hundred fifteen point seven million dollars in its first day. Guinness World Records called it the highest revenue ever for an entertainment product in twenty-four hours. It passed a billion dollars in three days. Faster than any movie, ever.
On November nineteenth, Grand Theft Auto Six comes out. Thirteen years later. And the money around it is already insane.

So how much could GTA Six make? Will America really call in sick to play it? And stay to the end, because I'll show you what happened to ten dollars a day in the company behind it, since GTA Five came out. The answer is not what you'd guess.

First, the price. Seventy-nine ninety-nine for the standard game. Ninety-nine ninety-nine for the Ultimate Edition. That's ten dollars more than most big games. One report estimated that the extra ten dollars alone could bring in about four hundred fifty million dollars more in the first year. And GTA Five, remember, has sold more than two hundred thirty million copies, according to Take-Two.

And here's the wild part. According to Sensor Tower, by October about six and a half million copies were already pre-ordered. Roughly six hundred thirty million dollars, before a single person has played it. Most buyers chose the hundred-dollar version.

Okay. How big could launch week get? Analysts cited by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier expect more than three billion dollars in the first four months. Morningstar projects sixty to seventy million copies in Take-Two's fiscal year.

Put that next to Hollywood. The biggest movie opening weekend of all time, Avengers Endgame, made about one point two billion dollars worldwide. GTA Five beat Avengers-level numbers thirteen years ago. GTA Six starts with a bigger fan base, a higher price, and six and a half million copies already sold.
Now here's the part most headlines skip. You've probably seen the claim that GTA Six sick days will cost the US economy a billion dollars.

That number came from a report that later said its own source should not be credited, and no national study backs it. TheStreet redid the math with the same assumptions and got closer to four hundred million. Still a lot of people pretending to have the flu.
So here's a question. When a giant game launches, does the stock go up? Let's check Take-Two after its biggest moments.
